subject: Ironclad vs DocuSign — feature gap analysis & recommendation needed
messages:
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Ironclad vs DocuSign — feature gap analysis & recommendation needed

Hi Marissa / Markus,

Quick context: our current DocuSign enterprise contract (e-sign only) is up for renewal in Q4. Over the last 6 months the Applied ML and Legal teams have been trialing Ironclad for CLM (workflows + redlines). We asked SRE/Platform to run a feature/cost comparison and the attached spreadsheet summarizes gaps and a preliminary TCO.

Options on the table:
- Keep DocuSign for signing, renew at current tier (minimal integration work)
- Migrate signing to Ironclad (consolidate CLM + e-sign) — one vendor, potential savings but migration risk and some missing advanced signature workflows
- Dual-vendor (Ironclad CLM + DocuSign for complex sig flows) — more complexity, higher ops cost

Key asks:
1) Marissa — any legal or compliance blockers you see from a CLM + e-sign consolidation? Data residency? audit-log retention? contract language we must keep?
2) Markus — do we have budget headroom to experiment with a consolidation (year 1 migration costs + year 2 run-rate)?
3) I recommend we give procurement the go-ahead to negotiate a consolidation scenario with Ironclad subject to Marissa's legal sign-off and a hard cap of $200k additional migration spend this FY.

Attachments: Ironclad_vs_DocuSign_feature_gap.xlsx, procurement_memo_20260809.pdf

I'll schedule a 30m sync if helpful — otherwise please reply with your take.

Thanks,
Grace

--

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Aug 2026 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Ironclad vs DocuSign — feature gap analysis & recommendation needed

Thanks Grace — good summary. I scanned the matrix and have a few legal/contract items to flag before consolidation: 

1) Signature evidentiary chain: DocuSign's default audit trail currently meets our procurement/legal standard for certain regulated agreements (we have a handful of EU financial partners). If we move to Ironclad e-sign, we need a clause preserving the audit chain format and exportability for at least 7 years.

2) Data residency & access: Ironclad has EU nodes but we need explicit contractual guarantees about where signed documents and copies of executed contracts are stored. Add explicit certifications (SOC 2 + ISO27001) to SLRs, and a right to audit clause.

3) Subprocessor list / notification window: need 30 days' notice of subprocessor changes and a covenant that critical subprocessors (CDN/KMS) cannot be replaced without prior approval for a period after execution.

4) Termination / export: ensure export hooks in machine-readable form (CSV + PDF) in the SOW and SLAs; require transition assistance for 90 days post-termination.

I can draft a rider that we can present to Ironclad as a minimum set of terms. If Ironclad is unwilling to accept these fixed obligations, we should consider a dual-vendor approach for the EU/regulatory subset.

Please share the procurement memo; I will add the legal redline attachment.

Marissa

From: Emma Blake <emma@ironclad.co>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Aug 2026 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Ironclad vs DocuSign — feature gap analysis & recommendation needed

Hi Grace / Marissa — thanks for the thoughtful review and the spreadsheet — appreciate the level of detail.

Couple of quick replies from Ironclad:
- We've attached SOW_v2 which includes our proposed migration services (90-day migration plan + dedicated PM) and a 15% one-time migration discount if you sign before 2026-09-30.
- On audit trails: we can guarantee exportable CSV/PDF exports and will add the 7-year retention clause into the SOW as standard for enterprise plans.
- Data residency: we confirm EU data residency option and SOC 2 Type II + ISO27001 certification; we will provide current attestation docs on exec.
- Subprocessors: we can agree to a 30-day notice window for subprocessor changes and will list critical subprocessors in the contract.

Pricing note: consolidation estimated run-rate is ~ $180k/year (post discount) for equivalent seat counts + $45k one-time migration services (discounted). We can provide a worked TCO if helpful — copy attached.

Attachments: Ironclad_SOW_v2.pdf, Ironclad_TCO_consolidation.xlsx

Happy to jump on a short call to walk through the SOW.

Best,
Emma Blake
Enterprise Accounts — West
Ironclad
emma@ironclad.co
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Aug 2026 10:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Ironclad vs DocuSign — feature gap analysis & recommendation needed

Marissa — thanks for the legal checklist, that helps a lot. Emma — thanks for the quick concessions — the 7-year export + subprocessor notice + attestation solves most of our legal asks.

Cost delta summary (rounded):
- Current DocuSign renewal: $120k/year
- Ironclad consolidated run-rate (after discount): $180k/year
- One-time migration cost (Ironclad quoted): $45k (negotiable down to ~$30k if we limit PM scope)

Net incremental first-year cost: ~ $105k (includes migration). Year 2+ projected $60k incremental run-rate. Benefits: single vendor for CLM/workflows + e-sign, unified audits, fewer integrations to maintain. Risks: migration effort, minor feature gaps in a couple of advanced signature workflows (noted in the spreadsheet).

Markus — do we have headroom to cover the migration and incremental run-rate? If yes, I propose we direct procurement to accept the SOW subject to Marissa's final redline and a max migration spend of $50k. Proc team will try to negotiate a lower one-time fee and a 2-year price cap.

I've attached the procurement memo for your review. If approved, I'll cc procurement and Ironclad legal to start redlines.

Thanks,
Grace
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Aug 2026 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Ironclad vs DocuSign — feature gap analysis & recommendation needed

Approved to proceed. We have budget headroom in Platform FY26 for up to $125k of incremental first-year spend for strategic tool consolidation. Proceed with procurement negotiations, but keep migration capped at $50k as proposed and circle back if Ironclad's firm pricing materially differs.

Markus
